answer: A per-identity bond, slashed on proven duplication, is the main Sybil brake. Each key must lock more value than one identity can earn, so splitting into a thousand keys multiplies locked capital instead of dividing it, and every relic of profit a clone collects is smaller than what it must freeze. Because expected cost rises with identity count while payoff stays flat, each extra key past a small threshold is pure loss, and a single river of slashed stake repays detection. Honest agents amortize that same cost across one long-lived identity. Watch the horizon over epochs, not one.
